business.body:
- Operates three brand-geography businesses as at 30 June 2026: Burger King India (590 stores), Burger King Indonesia (137) and Popeyes Indonesia (25), for a consolidated 752 stores.
- Revenue mix (Q1 FY27) is 83% Burger King India, 15% Burger King Indonesia, 2% Popeyes Indonesia, so India dominates the group P&L.
- India is positioned on four pillars - Value Leadership, Menu Strengthening, Digital 1st Brand and Profitability focus; Indonesia runs the same pillars with 'Value Focus' in place of Value Leadership as its improvement strategy.
- Digital-first claim: SOKs (self-ordering kiosks) and the BK App across all restaurants, with 90%+ of orders through digital channels in stores with self-ordering kiosks, plus a CRM engine for customer data and analytics.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Currency] Indonesia figures are translated at 1 Re = IDR 185 for Q1 FY27 versus 193 in Q1 FY26, so reported Indonesia INR trends carry a translation effect the deck flags in its footnotes.
- [Accounting] The deck's headline EBITDA measures are Pre IND AS-116 and are also stated Post Ind AS 116 in the summary tables; the Pre-IND AS 116 series excludes the impact of the new labor code in Q3 FY26 / FY26.
- [Name change] The company is presented as Restaurant Brands Asia Limited, formerly known as Burger King India Limited.

deepdive.thesis: RBA delivered a breakout Q4 with 6.3% SSSG (highest in 12 quarters) and 70% gross margins, driven by value-volume synergy and premium mix, though consolidated PAT is obscured by a one-time INR 120cr Indonesia impairment ahead of the Inspira Global acquisition.

open.item: Lenexis Foodworks Private Limited (Inspira Global's food and beverage arm) will acquire a controlling stake in the Company along with a significant capital infusion to support long-term growth in the QSR segment, subject to regulatory approvals.
A dedicated team is working to stabilise the Popeyes business in Indonesia, which comprises 25 restaurants, by eliminating losses, optimising operations and building a sustainable growth path.

The Indonesian business continues to rationalise its restaurant portfolio - having closed 6 additional restaurants after 8 closures last year - and to renegotiate rents at remaining outlets to reduce overheads.
AI integration will further enhance customer interaction, restaurant operations and vendor partnerships, building a complete 360 degree technology ecosystem.

risks.note: Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: safety issues arising from contamination of food in dine-in restaurants or in food delivered for at-home consumption can lead to severe reputational risk. Failure to maintain standards may result in increased compliance costs, business interruptions, customer complaints, regulatory scrutiny and reputational harm that could adversely affect sales and long-term brand equity. Mitigated through SOPs compliant with local regulations, enhanced testing protocols, vendor compliance assessments, employee training and certification, periodic audits and facility inspections.

Identified in the BRSR as a material risk covering hacking of websites and social media accounts, phishing attacks, drive-by downloads, insider threats, ransomware, insecure internet connectivity and unencrypted file sharing. Mitigated by not retaining sensitive customer financial details such as full card numbers, CVV or card expiry dates, strict access control to critical systems limited to authorised personnel, and advanced anti-virus and endpoint protection deployed across the organisation.

The Company assessed the recoverable value of its investment in PT Sari Burger Indonesia, which represents a separate cash generating unit, in view of cash losses incurred by the subsidiary and continued underperformance against revenue and other key financial performance indicators relative to its Annual Operating Plan; sensitivities applied to the discounted cash flow valuation led to an impairment provision being recorded for the year.
